scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapter 2 (with Online Appendix A1.1): An intertemporal model. The environment and household problem (Euler equation, money dominated when i > 0, no negative rates); the valuation equation derived from flow plus transversality for signed surpluses, with the transversality condition and the Euler equation derived from optimisation under uncertainty on finite event trees; existence and uniqueness of the price level; equilibrium formation and the money-overhang condition; fiscal and monetary policy: unexpected inflation determined by present-value news, interest-rate pegs, the expected/unexpected decomposition, share splits and equity issues, s-shaped surpluses, the flat supply curve; the linear fiscal theory of monetary policy (exact Fisher equation, peg and Taylor-type rule solutions for every theta, impulse responses); links to Woodford's exogenous-rate indeterminacy and Taylor principle.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapter 2, pp. 20-51, and Online Appendix A1.1, pp. 554-556.
